Join a world-class team of skilled engineers who build creative digital solutions to support our colleagues and clients. About this role
:
Software Development position responsible for design, implementation, and support of Python based web applications to help fulfill our Consulting & Insights Technology strategy.

Designing, implementing, unit, integration testing and supporting Python based applications and services

2+ years' experience in software development with full stack web applications development experience.
Strong knowledge of Python programming language experience
Hands on experience with Django, Flask or other Python frameworks
Strong experience with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and jQuery
Experience with either AWS OR ReactJs
Experience with relational databases using SQL (SQLServer, MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.)
Good problem-solving skills
Nice to have

Excellent communication and prioritization skills.
Able to work independently or within a team proactively in a fast-paced AGILE-SCRUM environment.
Owns success – Takes responsibility for successful delivery of the solutions.
Strong desire to improve upon their skills in software development, frameworks, and technologies

Competitive compensation.
Limitless growth and learning opportunities.

A chance to make an impact – your work will contribute directly to our strategy.

20+ PTO days plus holidays and floating holidays in your first year.

Tuition reimbursement.

Employee Assistance Program.

Who are we?
At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.
Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.
Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.
What makes Gartner a great place to work?
Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.
We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.
Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.
We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.
Gartner is the world authority on AI
At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.
It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.
What do we offer?
Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.
In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Build the Platforms That Power Enterprise Innovation
Are you passionate about automation, cloud engineering, and building modern software delivery platforms? Do you enjoy solving complex technical challenges while enabling development teams to deliver secure, scalable, and resilient applications?

description_preview:
Who We Are
Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.
About The Role
As an engineer at Notion, you’ll help shape core user experiences and accelerate how people discover value in Notion. You'll tackle meaningful challenges with increasing autonomy, crafting code that millions of users will experience. You'll take ownership of projects that matter, make critical technical decisions, and contribute your unique perspective to our product vision. Working alongside passionate experts across design, product, and data, you'll help shape the future of how people work.
We're looking for an Early Career AI Engineer to join as a strategic partner in shaping Notion's AI vision. You'll work on cutting-edge AI-powered features, leveraging LLMs, embeddings, and other AI technologies to make Notion more intelligent and capable.
Role
This role may be aligned to one of multiple AI-focused teams at Notion. Depending on team match and business needs, you could work on:
AI product engineering: building model-powered features end-to-end (UX, APIs, retrieval, orchestration, quality, and reliability)
Model & systems engineering: improving model integration and performance (latency, cost, safety, robustness) and building the infrastructure that supports model serving and experimentation
Evaluation & quality (evals): creating evaluation frameworks and automated/ human-in-the-loop testing to measure and improve model and product quality
What You’ll Achieve
Partner with your team to prototype and ship an AI-powered product improvement
Own a scoped productionization project: integrate a new model/technique into an existing workflow, add monitoring + guardrails, or improve latency/cost/reliability.
Contribute to evals and iteration loops: build or extend an evaluation set, run experiments, analyze results, and translate learnings into product or system changes.
Skills You'll Need To Bring
You have less than two years of engineering experience. You have solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems, with a customer-minded, pragmatic approach to solving problems.
Expertise building and prototyping: You’re excited to build and iterate quickly, and you’ve started exploring AI/ML through coursework, projects, internships, or hackathons. You’re comfortable learning how different parts of a product fit together (UI, APIs, data), have some familiarity with relational databases like Postgres or MySQL, and can take an idea from prototype to a working feature with guidance.
Thoughtful problem-solving: You approach problems holistically, starting with a clear and accurate understanding of the context. You think about the implications of what you're building and how it will impact real people's lives. You can navigate ambiguity successfully, decompose complex problems into clean solutions, while also balancing the business impact of what you’re building.
Impact-driven approach to technology: You see technologies as tools to achieve user impact rather than ends in themselves. You care more about building successful systems that solve real problems than about using specific tech stacks or following trends. You stay current with the latest tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and other AI-assisted development environments, you're pragmatic about choosing the right tool for the job, focusing on what delivers the most value to users and the business.
Proactive communication and high agency: You own your work, communicating clearly about progress and blockers. You don't wait for instructions for every step but rather show initiative in identifying what needs to be done and driving projects forward. You ask questions when needed while independently finding solutions to problems.
Nice to Haves
You have experience with any part of our technology stack: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Postgres, and Elasticsearch.
You care about the interaction between technology and society, the ways in which they inform each other, and our responsibility as technologists to be conscious of that relationship.
You've heard of computing pioneers like Ada Lovelace, Douglas Engelbart, Alan Kay, and others—and understand why we're big fans of their work.
Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco and New York, the estimated base salary range for this role is $130,000-$150,000.
By clicking “Submit Application”, I understand and agree that Notion and its affiliates and subsidiaries will collect and process my information in accordance with Notion’s Global Recruiting Privacy Policy.
A Note on AI
You don’t need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect every Notino to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it

description_preview:
Company Description
Peryx.ai is building an intelligence platform for renewable-energy operations. We transform complex industrial data into trusted, actionable insights that help teams make better operational decisions with confidence and human oversight.
About the role
We are looking for an
IoT & DevOps Engineer
to help build the initial data-ingestion and streaming foundation of the Peryx platform.
You will work across IoT connectivity, distributed data streaming, cloud infrastructure and platform reliability. The architecture will combine an
open-source-first technology stack
with selectively chosen partially and fully managed cloud services.
The ideal candidate is comfortable building systems hands-on, evaluating infrastructure trade-offs and operating reliable data pipelines in a fast-moving startup environment.
What you will build
You will contribute to an ingestion platform that:
Receives telemetry from solar plants, gateways and simulators.
Supports MQTT and HTTPS-based data ingestion.
Buffers and safely replays data during connectivity failures.
Moves high-volume events through MQTT brokers and streaming platforms.
Validates, deduplicates and routes incoming data.
Stores processed telemetry in operational databases.
Provides monitoring, inspection and observability across the complete pipeline.
Can gradually move between self-managed, partially managed and fully managed services as scale increases.
Key reponsibilities
Design, deploy and operate industrial data-ingestion infrastructure.
Configure and manage MQTT brokers such as EMQX or similar technologies.
Build and maintain Kafka-based event-streaming pipelines and bridge workers.
Evaluate and integrate technologies such as Apache Kafka, Apache NiFi and AWS Kinesis.
Containerize services using Docker and manage deployments using Kubernetes or equivalent orchestration platforms.
Build infrastructure and deployment automation for cloud and hybrid environments.
Configure high availability, load balancing, replication, retries and failure recovery.
Manage PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB or similar operational databases.
Implement secure device and service communication using MQTT, HTTPS and TLS.
Establish monitoring using tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Kafka UI/Kafbat and message-inspection utilities.
Support capacity planning, performance testing, incident investigation and production troubleshooting.
Document architectural decisions, operational procedures and deployment workflows.
Collaborate with backend, data and domain teams to define reliable ingestion contracts.
Required experience
Practical experience with Linux, networking and cloud infrastructure.
Strong understanding of Docker and containerized deployments.
Working knowledge of Kubernetes and distributed application operations.
Experience with at least one major cloud provider, preferably AWS.
Basic understanding of data-streaming concepts such as topics, partitions, consumers, offsets, retention, replay and delivery guarantees.
Familiarity with Apache Kafka and the broader Apache data ecosystem.
Experience managing relational databases such as PostgreSQL.
Understanding of CI/CD, infrastructure automation, logging, monitoring and alerting.
Ability to troubleshoot failures across applications, networks, containers and databases.
Demonstrated experience working with open-source technologies.
Open-source expectation
Candidates should have either:
Contributed code, documentation, testing or issue resolutions to an open-source project; or
Meaningful hands-on experience deploying, extending or operating open-source infrastructure.
Please include links to relevant GitHub repositories, pull requests, technical articles or community contributions where available.
Good to have
Experience with MQTT brokers such as EMQX, Mosquitto or HiveMQ.
Understanding of MQTT QoS, persistent sessions, retained messages and topic design.
Experience with Apache NiFi, Kafka Connect, Kafka Streams or AWS Kinesis.
Knowledge of HAProxy, NGINX or similar load-balancing technologies.
Experience with PostgreSQL time-series workloads or TimescaleDB.
Understanding of local buffering, ordered replay, idempotency and deduplication.
Exposure to industrial IoT, SCADA, solar-energy systems, manufacturing or utility telemetry.
Experience ingesting data from devices, gateways, PLCs, meters, inverters or weather-monitoring systems.
Knowledge of Terraform, Helm, GitOps or infrastructure-as-code practices.
Familiarity with managed Kafka, container and database services on AWS.
What success looks like
During the initial phase, you will help Peryx establish a secure and observable ingestion layer capable of receiving industrial telemetry, surviving temporary failures, replaying buffered data and reliably delivering events for downstream processing.
The system should be easy to operate today while providing a clear path to scale and adopt managed services where they create meaningful operational value.
Who will succeed in the role
You will be a strong fit if you:
Enjoy building infrastructure rather than only configuring vendor products.
Can make practical trade-offs between reliability, cost and complexity.
Are comfortable working with incomplete requirements and converting them into working systems.
Prefer evidence, testing and observability over assumptions.
Take ownership of systems from initial design through deployment and production operation.
Why join Peryx
You will help build the foundational infrastructure behind an industrial intelligence platform from an early stage. Your decisions will directly shape how renewable-energy data is collected, protected, processed and scaled across the platform.

We Are
Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.
You Are
You have spent your career making code run faster on hardware that keeps changing. You understand that the difference between a solver that takes three hours and one that takes twenty minutes is not just compute power, it is how the algorithm maps to memory, how threads communicate, and whether someone thought hard about cache locality six months ago. You know your way around a profiler and you can read the output without needing to Google every metric.
Working across CPU and GPU architectures does not intimidate you. You have debugged MPI communication bottlenecks, wrestled with build systems that span multiple platforms, and written code that has to perform consistently whether it is running on a local workstation or a cloud-based HPC cluster. You think in terms of scalability, not just correctness.
Collaboration comes naturally. You can sit with a domain expert who speaks in finite elements and boundary conditions, extract what matters for the code, and turn that into a design spec that your team can actually build from. You care about the engineers downstream who depend on your work holding up under real-world load, not just passing CI.
At Synopsys, you will work on simulation software that shapes how products get designed across industries. The problems are real, the scale is significant, and what you optimize will matter.
What You'll Be Doing
Design, implement, and optimize parallel programming methods within Ansys Mechanical solver products using MPI, GPU programming models like CUDA, HIP, SYCL, OpenMP, and other HPC frameworks
Profile solver performance across CPU and GPU architectures using tools like Intel VTune, NVIDIA Nsight, or similar, and translate findings into actionable performance improvements

Drive adoption of modular, hardware-agnostic HPC programming models across multiple solver codebases, working with development teams to ensure consistency and reusability
Collaborate with numerical methods experts to translate complex algorithmic requirements into performant, maintainable software designs

Reduce solve times for engineering simulations used by leading companies across automotive, aerospace, energy, and electronics industries
Enable customers to run larger, more complex models by making solvers scale efficiently across hundreds or thousands of cores
Accelerate the adoption of GPU computing in production simulation workflows, unlocking new performance tiers for users with modern hardware
Improve developer productivity across multiple solver teams by building reusable HPC frameworks and shared tooling

What You'll Need
Minimum Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Computational Science, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or related field with 2+ years of experience, or Master's degree in a related field. PhD preferred.

Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, and performance considerations in parallel computing contexts

You can look at a profiler trace and identify the bottleneck without needing three meetings to discuss it
You write code that other engineers can pick up six months later without needing you to explain every design choice
You ask clarifying questions when a requirement is vague rather than guessing and building the wrong thing
You are comfortable managing your own time across multiple priorities and know when to escalate blockers versus solve them yourself
You can explain a technical tradeoff between two HPC approaches to a domain expert in terms they care about, not just what the benchmark says
You stay current with HPC architecture trends and programming models without needing to be told, because you care about building software that will still perform well two hardware generations from now

You will work within the Ansys Mechanical R&D organization, collaborating with numerical methods experts, solver developers, and other HPC engineers across a geographically distributed team. description_preview:
Who We Are
Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.
Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.
About The Role
As an Early Career Software Engineer at Notion, you’ll help shape core user experiences and accelerate how people discover value in Notion. You'll tackle meaningful challenges with increasing autonomy, crafting code that millions of users will experience. You'll take ownership of projects that matter, make critical technical decisions, and contribute your unique perspective to our product vision. Working alongside passionate experts across design, product, and data, you'll help shape the future of how people work.
We’re hiring early career engineers to join us across several teams at Notion. Your recruiter will partner with you to find the team that aligns best with your interests and where you can make the highest impact.
What You’ll Achieve
Plan, build, and ship product features from conception to launch, then iterate based on insights and customer feedback.
Improve performance, reliability, and quality of key experiences used by millions of users and thousands of organizations.
Run experiments that drive activation, retention, collaboration, and revenue, partnering with design, data science, and research.
Build internal tools and platform improvements that help all engineers ship quickly and safely.
Contribute to team norms, code quality, and a culture of learning and thoughtful tradeoffs.
Areas you might work on
Core Notion product features: Help develop, improve, and maintain features for our flagship product, focusing on the editor, databases, sharing, or other key areas that power millions of workflows.
AI and automation: Help develop and integrate intelligent features that make Notion more powerful, contextual, and efficient for our users.
Growth and activation: Work on features that help new users discover Notion's value, improve onboarding experiences, and increase user engagement.
Platform and infrastructure: Contribute to the systems that power Notion's backend services, ensuring reliability, scalability, and performance as our user base grows.
Skills You'll Need To Bring
You have less than two years of engineering experience. You have solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems, with a customer-minded, pragmatic approach to solving problems.
Thoughtful problem-solving: You approach problems holistically, starting with a clear and accurate understanding of the context. You think about the implications of what you're building and how it will impact real people's lives. You can navigate ambiguity successfully, decompose complex problems into clean solutions, while also balancing the business impact of what you’re building.
Impact-driven approach to technology: You see technologies as tools to achieve user impact rather than ends in themselves. You care more about building successful systems that solve real problems than about using specific tech stacks or following trends. You stay current with the latest tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and other AI-assisted development environments, you're pragmatic about choosing the right tool for the job, focusing on what delivers the most value to users and the business.
Proactive communication and high agency: You own your work, communicating clearly about progress and blockers. You don't wait for instructions for every step but rather show initiative in identifying what needs to be done and driving projects forward. You ask questions when needed while independently finding solutions to problems.
Nice to Haves
You have experience with any part of our technology stack: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Postgres, and Elasticsearch.
You care about the interaction between technology and society, the ways in which they inform each other, and our responsibility as technologists to be conscious of that relationship.
You've heard of computing pioneers like Ada Lovelace, Douglas Engelbart, Alan Kay, and others—and understand why we're big fans of their work.

Camus enables flexible grid connections that allow new load and generation to connect sooner by planning for and operating within real system constraints. Our platform bridges the gap between grid operators and large load developers such as data centers, providing a view of time-varying grid capacity for any given new interconnection point.
We combine high-reliability software experience from companies like Google and Meta with deep power systems expertise across the utility sector. If you’re excited to work at the intersection of infrastructure, software, and climate, we’d love to hear from you.

We take that responsibility seriously, and we want someone whose maturity managing data systems is commensurate with that.

Entangl is building the operating system for critical infrastructure, starting with data centers.
We turn fragmented drawings, documentation, telemetry, alarms, procedures, and operational knowledge into a system that helps teams understand what is happening, identify problems, and operate facilities safely.
We are looking for an exceptional Frontend Engineer to build the interfaces through which operators interact with complex physical infrastructure.
This is not a role for someone who only converts Figma files into components.
You will be expected to understand the user, question the workflow, simplify complex information, make sound product decisions, and take complete ownership of what reaches the customer.
Our customers operate facilities where confusion, missing information, and poor usability have real consequences. The product must be fast, clear, reliable, and exceptionally easy to use; even when the underlying systems are complicated.
What You Will Build
You may work on:
Interactive electrical and mechanical system diagrams.
Interfaces for navigating complex data center infrastructure.
Real-time telemetry, alarms, abnormalities, and operational issues.
Workflows for diagnosing and resolving equipment problems.
Procedure-generation and execution tools.
Interfaces for validating asset data and customer documentation.
Dashboards used by operators, engineers, executives, and customers.
Tools that allow Entangl to be deployed and configured quickly across many sites.
Systems that adapt to different customers, facilities, asset types, and data sources.
Internal tools that allow our team to move faster without compromising quality.
The challenge is not simply displaying information. It is deciding what matters, how it should be structured, and how to help a user take the correct action quickly.
What You Will Own
Build polished, production-quality frontend features from concept to deployment.
Take ownership of entire user workflows, not isolated tickets.
Work directly with customers and internal domain experts to understand operational problems.
Translate complex engineering concepts into interfaces that feel simple and intuitive.

reason: Stack +8; Title fit +6; US +10
description_preview:
About Stackbirds
Most small businesses are run by people who are great at the thing they do and stuck doing everything else. The bookkeeping, the follow-ups, the quotes, the scheduling, the hundred small operational decisions a day that never made it into why they started. Big companies have teams and systems for all of it. Everyone else has nights and weekends.
Stackbirds is building the platform where a small business comes to run their business. One place that handles the operational weight, so the people doing skilled work can stay focused on the work. We're early, we have real businesses using us, and we're partnered with universities embedding our platform into how the next generation learns to run a company.
The founder previously built and exited companies and held senior product and engineering roles at Meta, Airbnb, and Canva. The throughline across everything she's built: tools for skilled people who don't have the business infrastructure that bigger players take for granted.
The role
As Founding Engineer, you'll build the technical foundation of that platform alongside the founder. This is a build-from-the-ground-up role: you'll make the early architecture decisions, ship the first production systems, and help shape what the engineering team becomes. You'll work directly with the businesses we serve, so you'll see what you build land in someone's actual day.
This is for someone who wants the scope and ownership of a founding seat, and who's drawn to the problem of giving small businesses the kind of infrastructure that used to require a whole team.
What you'll do
Build the core platform that small businesses rely on to run their day-to-day operations.
Make foundational calls on architecture, infrastructure, tooling, and the engineering stack.
Ship end to end — from the systems underneath to the experience a business owner actually touches.
Work directly with the businesses using Stackbirds and turn what you learn into product.
Set the early engineering culture, standards, and hiring bar as the team grows.
What we're looking for
Strong full-stack or backend engineering experience, with a track record of shipping production systems end to end.
Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward shipping; you can go from a rough problem to a working system without a spec handed to you.
Product instinct — you care about who you're building for and what their day is like, not just the architecture.
Genuine interest in small businesses and the people who run them.
Readiness to take on founding-level ownership and scope.
Nice to have
Experience as an early engineer at a startup.
Background in tools for small businesses, operations, fintech, or B2B SaaS.
Experience standing up infrastructure and deployment pipelines from scratch.
Fluency with modern AI tooling as a means to build a better product, not as the product itself.
What we offer
Founding equity and meaningful ownership.
Direct partnership with the founder and a real say in technical direction.
The chance to build a company's technical foundation from day one.
How to apply
Send a note on what you've built and why this role fits, along with your GitHub, portfolio, or anything that shows your work. Email engineering@stackbird.xyz.

We are seeking a system software engineer to develop low-level diagnostic software for next-generation data center GPUs and rack-scale AI systems. Our team builds software that exercises and validates complex hardware, including compute engines, memory and cache subsystems, NICs, PCIe and NVLink interfaces, power delivery, and thermal behavior. This role is well suited to an embedded, firmware, device-driver, hardware-validation, or systems software engineer who enjoys working close to hardware.
